title: UPCAT Skill Tree
subtitle: A left-to-right study path for the University of the Philippines College Admission Test.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.blurb: Arithmetic, algebra, geometry, and data — rebuilt from the ground up for timed problem solving.

nodes.title: Start Here
nodes.description: Take a short diagnostic across arithmetic, algebra, and geometry. Clear this node to open the first arithmetic milestone.
nodes.tip: Log each miss by topic; your weakest three topics become the first subskills you study.

nodes.title: Operations & Number Sense
nodes.description: Integer rules, order of operations, divisibility, primes, and the number properties UPCAT leans on.
nodes.tip: Drill 20 order-of-operations items daily; write each step instead of computing in your head.

nodes.title: Fractions, Decimals & Percents
nodes.description: Convert fluently between forms and handle percent change, discounts, and fractional parts.
nodes.tip: Memorize the fraction–percent table (1/8 = 12.5%, 1/6 ≈ 16.7%) so you can skip long division.

nodes.title: Ratios & Proportions
nodes.description: Part-to-part and part-to-whole ratios, direct and inverse proportion, and scaling.
nodes.tip: When a problem gives a ratio, assign a multiplier x and express every quantity in terms of x.

nodes.title: Estimation & Mental Math
nodes.description: Approximate before you compute, sanity-check answer choices, and use friendly benchmarks.
nodes.tip: Round first. UPCAT choices are often far enough apart that an estimate eliminates three options.

nodes.title: Algebraic Expressions
nodes.description: Simplify expressions, combine like terms, expand, and translate words into algebra.
nodes.tip: Underline the unknown and write a 'let x =' line before touching the equation.

nodes.title: Linear Equations & Inequalities
nodes.description: Solve one- and two-variable linear equations, work with inequalities, and interpret slope.
nodes.tip: Whatever you do to one side, do to the other. Flip the inequality sign when multiplying by a negative.

nodes.title: Rates, Work & Mixture
nodes.description: Speed–distance–time, combined work, and mixture problems solved with clean tables.
nodes.tip: Use the units to decide the operation: 'of the job per hour' means your rates add.

nodes.title: Polynomials & Factoring
nodes.description: Expand, factor, and simplify polynomials including difference of squares and trinomials.
nodes.tip: Always check for a greatest common factor before trying any other factoring pattern.

nodes.title: Systems of Equations
nodes.description: Solve two-variable systems by substitution and elimination; recognize no-solution cases.
nodes.tip: Elimination is faster when coefficients line up — multiply to create opposites, then add.

nodes.title: Sequences & Series
nodes.description: Arithmetic and geometric sequences, nth terms, and simple series sums.
nodes.tip: List the first four terms before hunting for a formula — the pattern is usually visible.

nodes.title: Functions & Graphs
nodes.description: Function notation, domain and range, transformations, and graph interpretation.
nodes.tip: Test one input value to match a graph to an equation — faster than analyzing the whole shape.

nodes.title: Lines, Angles & Triangles
nodes.description: Angle relationships, triangle properties, congruence, and the exterior angle theorem.
nodes.tip: Draw the figure even when one is provided, and mark every given value on it.

nodes.title: Coordinate Geometry
nodes.description: Distance, midpoint, slope, and equations of lines on the Cartesian plane.
nodes.tip: Sketch the points; most coordinate problems become obvious once the segment or triangle is drawn.

nodes.title: Circles, Area & Volume
nodes.description: Circle measures plus perimeter, area, surface area, and volume of solids.
nodes.tip: Keep a one-page formula sheet and re-derive it weekly so the formulas actually stick.

nodes.title: Averages & Weighted Mean
nodes.description: Mean, median, mode, range, and weighted averages in mixed data sets.
nodes.tip: For weighted mean, convert each weight into a fraction of the total before multiplying.

nodes.title: Timed Math Simulation
nodes.description: Full mixed math sets under the official time limit, followed by an error-log review.
nodes.tip: Simulate the real clock, then tag every miss by topic. Retake only your two weakest topics first.

nodes.title: Counting & Probability
nodes.description: Permutations, combinations, and single- and multi-event probability.
nodes.tip: Ask whether order matters: order matters → permutation, order does not → combination.

nodes.title: Quadratic Equations
nodes.description: Solve by factoring, completing the square, and the quadratic formula; read parabolas.
nodes.tip: Check the discriminant first; it tells you how many real roots to expect before you solve.

nodes.title: Data Interpretation
nodes.description: Read tables, bar graphs, and pie charts; compute rates and compare proportions.
nodes.tip: Read the axis labels and units before the question; most traps live in 'percent of what?'.

nodes.title: Advanced Word Problems
nodes.description: Translate multi-step age, digit, investment, and geometry word problems into equations.
nodes.tip: Write the final question as a sentence with a blank; it tells you exactly what to solve for.

nodes.title: Similarity & Right Triangles
nodes.description: Similar figures, Pythagorean triples, and basic right-triangle trigonometry.
nodes.tip: Memorize 3-4-5, 5-12-13, and 8-15-17 so you can skip the Pythagorean theorem on test day.

subjects.name: Science
subjects.blurb: Biology, chemistry, physics, and earth science compressed into the concepts UPCAT actually repeats.

nodes.title: Start Here
nodes.description: Take a short mixed-science diagnostic covering biology, chemistry, physics, and earth science. Clear this node to open the first science milestone.
nodes.tip: Sort every miss by branch, then start with the branch that has the most misses.

nodes.title: Scientific Method & Measurement
nodes.description: Hypotheses, variables, controlled experiments, and SI units with significant figures.
nodes.tip: For any experiment question, identify the independent variable first — it anchors everything else.

nodes.title: Cell Structure & Function
nodes.description: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, organelles, membranes, and transport.
nodes.tip: Link each organelle to a factory job; function questions outnumber structure questions.

nodes.title: Matter & Its Properties
nodes.description: States of matter, physical vs chemical changes, mixtures, and separation techniques.
nodes.tip: Classify first: if a new substance forms, the change is chemical.

nodes.title: Earth's Structure & Rocks
nodes.description: Layers of the Earth, the rock cycle, minerals, and soil formation.
nodes.tip: Sketch the rock cycle once from memory; most items test transitions, not definitions.

nodes.title: Forces & Equilibrium
nodes.description: Types of forces, free-body diagrams, friction, and balanced vs unbalanced systems.
nodes.tip: Draw the free-body diagram before choosing an equation; never skip the normal force.

nodes.title: Chemical Bonding
nodes.description: Ionic vs covalent bonds, Lewis structures, and intermolecular forces.
nodes.tip: Metal + nonmetal is ionic; nonmetal + nonmetal is covalent. That one rule answers many items.

nodes.title: Atomic Structure & Periodic Table
nodes.description: Subatomic particles, electron configuration, and periodic trends.
nodes.tip: Trends follow position: radius grows down and left; electronegativity grows up and right.

nodes.title: Plate Tectonics & Earthquakes
nodes.description: Plate boundaries, fault types, seismic waves, and volcanoes.
nodes.tip: Divergent → ridge, convergent → trench or mountain, transform → fault. Match boundary to landform.

nodes.title: Motion & Newton's Laws
nodes.description: Kinematics graphs, acceleration, and Newton's three laws applied to real systems.
nodes.tip: In a velocity–time graph, slope is acceleration and area under the line is displacement.

nodes.title: Reactions & Stoichiometry
nodes.description: Balancing equations, reaction types, moles, and limiting reactants.
nodes.tip: Balance oxygen and hydrogen last; leave the most complex formula for the final count.

nodes.title: Human Body Systems
nodes.description: Circulation, respiration, digestion, excretion, and nervous coordination.
nodes.tip: Trace one oxygen molecule and one glucose molecule through the body; most items follow those paths.

nodes.title: Genetics & Heredity
nodes.description: DNA, Mendelian crosses, Punnett squares, and pedigree analysis.
nodes.tip: For dihybrid crosses, split the problem into two monohybrid crosses and multiply.

nodes.title: Weather, Climate & Oceans
nodes.description: Atmosphere layers, fronts, storms, ocean currents, and climate patterns.
nodes.tip: Low pressure means rising air and rain; high pressure means sinking air and fair weather.

nodes.title: Ecology & Evolution
nodes.description: Food webs, population dynamics, natural selection, and biodiversity.
nodes.tip: Removing a top predator cascades downward; trace the chain two steps before answering.

nodes.title: Science Simulation
nodes.description: Mixed science sets under time pressure with error-log review.
nodes.tip: Log every miss by topic; revisit the weakest branch before the next simulation.

nodes.title: Work, Energy & Momentum
nodes.description: Work, power, conservation of energy, and collisions.
nodes.tip: Check whether the system is closed; if it is, mechanical energy at the start equals the end.

nodes.title: Waves, Light & Electricity
nodes.description: Wave properties, reflection and refraction, circuits, and Ohm's law.
nodes.tip: For circuits, find total resistance first, then total current, then branch values.

nodes.title: Solar System & the Universe
nodes.description: Planets, seasons, tides, stars, and the Big Bang.
nodes.tip: Seasons come from axial tilt, not distance from the Sun — a classic UPCAT trap.

subjects.name: Language Proficiency
subjects.blurb: Grammar, vocabulary, and usage rules that appear again and again in the language section.

nodes.title: Start Here
nodes.description: Take a short language diagnostic on grammar, vocabulary, and usage. Clear this node to open the first language milestone.
nodes.tip: Mark the rule behind every error, not just the answer you missed.

nodes.title: Sentence Fundamentals
nodes.description: Subjects, predicates, phrases, clauses, and the anatomy of a complete sentence.
nodes.tip: Find the verb first, then ask who or what is doing it — the subject appears quickly.

nodes.title: Parts of Speech
nodes.description: Nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, prepositions, and how a word's role shifts by sentence.
nodes.tip: Identify the word's job, not its dictionary category; the same word can be noun or verb.

nodes.title: Word Roots & Context Clues
nodes.description: Prefixes, suffixes, common roots, and using surrounding text to infer meaning.
nodes.tip: Build a 30-root deck (bene, mal, chron, graph, spect) and review it in five-minute bursts.

nodes.title: Subject–Verb Agreement
nodes.description: Singular and plural agreement with tricky subjects, collective nouns, and inverted sentences.
nodes.tip: Cross out prepositional phrases between the subject and verb; they hide the real subject.

nodes.title: Verb Tenses & Forms
nodes.description: Perfect tenses, active vs passive voice, and consistency across a passage.
nodes.tip: Look for time markers (since, by the time, already); they identify the perfect tense almost every time.

nodes.title: Synonyms & Antonyms
nodes.description: Shades of meaning, precise word choice, and elimination by connotation.
nodes.tip: Sort choices from most positive to most negative; the outlier is usually the trap.

nodes.title: Punctuation & Mechanics
nodes.description: Commas, semicolons, colons, dashes, and capitalization rules that get tested often.
nodes.tip: A semicolon joins two complete sentences; if either side cannot stand alone, use a comma instead.

nodes.title: Modifiers & Parallelism
nodes.description: Misplaced and dangling modifiers plus parallel structure in lists and comparisons.
nodes.tip: Ask what a modifier is describing; if the answer is not the nearest noun, it is misplaced.

nodes.title: Rhetoric & Tone
nodes.description: Author's attitude, persuasion techniques, and register shifts in nonfiction.
nodes.tip: Tone lives in adjectives and adverbs; circle them before choosing an answer.

nodes.title: Idioms & Analogies
nodes.description: Common idioms, preposition pairings, and bridge-building for analogy items.
nodes.tip: Write the analogy as a sentence before reading the choices; match the relationship, not the topic.

nodes.title: Pronoun Reference & Case
nodes.description: Pronoun–antecedent agreement, ambiguous references, and nominative vs objective case.
nodes.tip: Replace each pronoun with its supposed noun; the sentence will expose ambiguity instantly.

nodes.title: Figures of Speech
nodes.description: Simile, metaphor, personification, hyperbole, irony, and rhetorical devices.
nodes.tip: Label the comparison first; if it uses like or as it is a simile, otherwise test for direct substitution.

nodes.title: Language Simulation
nodes.description: Full language section under time with targeted error review.
nodes.tip: Keep an error log by rule type; most students lose the same three points repeatedly.

nodes.title: Sentence Combining & Flow
nodes.description: Combine choppy sentences and choose the most concise, logical arrangement.
nodes.tip: Prefer the shortest option that keeps every original idea; extra words are usually wrong.

nodes.title: Vocabulary in Context
nodes.description: Choose the meaning that fits the passage, including figurative and technical uses.
nodes.tip: Substitute each choice into the sentence and read it aloud in your head; awkwardness eliminates options.

nodes.title: Precision & Register
nodes.description: Formal vs informal diction, connotation, and eliminating wordiness.
nodes.tip: Formal writing avoids contractions, slang, and 'you'; use that to eliminate choices fast.

subjects.name: Reading Comprehension
subjects.blurb: Read faster, map arguments, and recognize the trap types that make reading items feel subjective.

nodes.title: Start Here
nodes.description: Take one timed short passage and note where you lose time or accuracy. Clear this node to open the first reading milestone.
nodes.tip: Time the passage, then classify each miss as a detail, inference, or trap answer.

nodes.title: Main Idea & Theme
nodes.description: Distinguish topic, main idea, and theme across paragraphs and whole passages.
nodes.tip: State the passage's point in one sentence before looking at the choices.

nodes.title: Active Reading & Annotation
nodes.description: Read with purpose: mark claims, turns, and names instead of highlighting everything.
nodes.tip: Annotate the margin with two or three words per paragraph; it makes questions locatable.

nodes.title: Vocabulary in Context
nodes.description: Infer word meaning from syntax, contrast, and examples inside the passage.
nodes.tip: Cover the word and predict a substitute from the sentence, then match your prediction to the options.

nodes.title: Supporting Details
nodes.description: Locate explicit evidence and distinguish it from plausible but unsupported claims.
nodes.tip: Every detail answer must be provable by a specific line; no line, no selection.

nodes.title: Text Structure & Organization
nodes.description: Chronology, cause and effect, comparison, problem-solution, and their signposts.
nodes.tip: Map the passage's skeleton (each paragraph's purpose) rather than its content.

nodes.title: Inference & Implication
nodes.description: Draw only the conclusions the text forces, not ones that are merely possible.
nodes.tip: Ask 'does the passage have to mean this?' If not, eliminate the choice.

nodes.title: Compare & Contrast Passages
nodes.description: Handle paired passages by mapping agreements and disagreements first.
nodes.tip: Build a two-column table for paired passages before answering; shared claims are common answers.

nodes.title: Critical Reading & Bias
nodes.description: Evaluate evidence, assumptions, and persuasive framing in an argument.
nodes.tip: Find the unstated assumption: it is the bridge between evidence and conclusion.

nodes.title: Author's Purpose & Tone
nodes.description: Identify why the author writes and how attitude shapes word choice.
nodes.tip: Separate purpose (why) from tone (how it sounds); they are usually two different questions.

nodes.title: Question-Type Strategy
nodes.description: Match question stems to the right reading approach and predicted answer.
nodes.tip: Read the question stem before the answer choices; predicting first prevents trap answers.

nodes.title: Reading Simulation
nodes.description: Timed multi-passage practice with error analysis.
nodes.tip: Review wrong answers by naming the trap type, not just the correct letter.

nodes.title: Elimination Tactics
nodes.description: Recognize extreme, out-of-scope, and true-but-irrelevant distractors.
nodes.tip: Cross out choices with absolutes (always, never, all) unless the passage states them plainly.

nodes.title: Passage Mapping & Timing
nodes.description: Budget minutes per passage and decide when to move on.
nodes.tip: Cap each passage at its budget; flag one hard question and return only if time remains.

subjects.name: Essay Writing
subjects.blurb: The UPCAT essay rewards a clear position and concrete evidence more than flowery prose.

nodes.title: Start Here
nodes.description: Read three essay prompts and write a five-minute outline for one without notes. Clear this node to open the first writing milestone.
nodes.tip: Plan before you write; a five-minute outline is the cheapest score you can buy.

nodes.title: Brainstorm & Outline
nodes.description: Generate a position, two or three supports, and a counterpoint in five minutes.
nodes.tip: Use a three-line skeleton: claim, two reasons, one objection. Fill in details while writing.

nodes.title: Decode the Prompt
nodes.description: Identify the task, scope, and key terms before planning a response.
nodes.tip: Underline the instruction verb and the limits; a response that ignores scope is capped early.

nodes.title: Choose Your Mode
nodes.description: Decide quickly between a personal narrative and an argumentative response, then commit to one structure.
nodes.tip: Pick the mode that fits the prompt's verb; switching halfway wastes the most time.

nodes.title: Thesis & Position
nodes.description: Write a specific, arguable thesis that answers the prompt directly.
nodes.tip: Put the thesis in the last sentence of your introduction and echo it in the conclusion.

nodes.title: Evidence & Examples
nodes.description: Use concrete, relevant examples, including Philippine and personal contexts.
nodes.tip: One well-explained example beats three name-drops; analysis earns the points.

nodes.title: Paragraph Architecture
nodes.description: Topic sentence, evidence, analysis, and a bridge to the next idea.
nodes.tip: Every body paragraph should be explainable by its topic sentence alone.

nodes.title: Transitions & Cohesion
nodes.description: Logical connectors and echo phrases that tie paragraphs into one argument.
nodes.tip: Transition with ideas, not just words: end a paragraph with the question the next one answers.

nodes.title: Style Polish
nodes.description: Rhythm, emphasis, and control of sentence length in a timed draft.
nodes.tip: Vary sentence openings; three sentences in a row with the same subject reads flat.

nodes.title: Voice & Word Choice
nodes.description: Clear, varied sentences and precise diction under exam conditions.
nodes.tip: Cut adverbs and 'very'; replace vague praise with specific verbs.

nodes.title: Counterargument & Nuance
nodes.description: Acknowledge the strongest objection and answer it without weakening your claim.
nodes.tip: Concede one real limitation, then explain why your position still holds.

nodes.title: Essay Simulation
nodes.description: Full-length timed essay with a self-scoring rubric.
nodes.tip: Score with the same rubric every time so improvements are actually comparable.

nodes.title: Timed Essay Practice
nodes.description: Plan, draft, and review a complete essay in the official time limit.
nodes.tip: Reserve the last five minutes for a read-through; fix agreement and tense errors first.

nodes.title: Conclusion & Final Impression
nodes.description: Close the argument by answering 'so what?' and linking back to the thesis without repeating it.
nodes.tip: End on the implication, not a summary; the last line is what the reader remembers.
